text:
alice: Heads-up — I ran an nsys capture on the q4-hosted pool after yesterday's batching tweak. Seeing a ~200–400ms tail on some 1→2 token requests. Perfetto trace: https://perfetto/trace/abcd (private). The odd part: kernel selector flips from fast_fp4_gemm to fallback_int8 for essentially identical calls when batch grows from 1 to 3. nvtx ranges are present but pretty coarse. Any ideas?

ben: :eyes: can you paste the nsys command you used and a snippet of the kernel timeline? also which batching commit hash?

alice: CLI I ran: `nsys profile --output /tmp/run.nsys --trace=nvtx,cuda --sample=none --duration=30s --capture-range=nvtx`
Kernel timeline (excerpt):
```
time  kernel_name               duration_ms  stream
0.123  fast_fp4_gemm             0.45         s1
0.578  fast_fp4_gemm             0.42         s1
1.105  fallback_int8_matmul      12.3         s1
1.140  fallback_int8_matmul      11.9         s1
```
These fallback rows line up with requests where batch moved 1→3 between iterations.

chao: That pattern screams KV-cache / prefetch boundary. If prefetch/prefix caching misses, we may materialize a longer effective seq_len and trigger different kernel thresholds. Do we have the selector thresholds table (seq_len/batch -> kernel)?

dana: I ran a quick microbench earlier: our selector currently picks fast_fp4_gemm for max_seq <= 16 and bsize <= 2; otherwise it chooses fallback_int8. The bug is we use ``max_seq`` from route config rather than the request's actual active sequence. So a b=3 request with short active tokens may still be forced into the fallback.

ben: We should add an NVTX range around the kernel decision point with attributes: batch_size, actual_seq, route_max_seq, quant_profile. That makes filtering traces for the selector decision trivial. Naming: short, parseable, and stable.

alice: I can add ranges — question on naming convention. Should we do `KS(decision)` or `KS:pick=...`? The trace parser needs deterministic splitting (no spaces).

chao: Use colon + comma format, no spaces. Example: `KS:pick=fast_fp4,b=3,aseq=12,rmx=64`. Keep under 64 chars. Also emit numerical attrs via nvtxRangeStartEx (batch, aseq, uid) so automated tooling can read ints instead of parsing strings.

dana: note — adding a lot of tiny NVTX ranges will blow up trace size and make capturing slower. Consider emitting a single per-request summary range (PR:summary) that contains a short decision blob instead of every sub-check. Or sample 1% of requests with full detail.

perf-bot: trace-size alert — `/tmp/run.nsys` is 1.2GB (capture 00:30) :warning: 

alice: Plan: 1) add `KS:` nvtx range at the selector exit with attrs (pick, b,aseq,rmx,profile) and a per-request root id; 2) run a focused microtrace with sampling disabled and `--capture-range=nvtx` and a 5s window capturing the problematic pool; 3) diff kernel_map between baseline and current (I will dump `selector.kernel_map` JSON). I'll open a draft PR with changes and a sampling flag so we don't always emit full attrs.

ben: +1. For the PR include an example perfetto query and a small python parser snippet to convert nvtx attrs into CSV. That will speed triage.

chao: quick snippet for NVTX push we can reuse:```c
nvtxEventAttributes_t attr = {0};
attr.version = NVTX_VERSION;
attr.size = NVTX_EVENT_ATTRIB_STRUCT_SIZE;
attr.messageType = NVTX_MESSAGE_TYPE_ASCII;
attr.message.ascii = "KS:pick=fast_fp4,b=3,aseq=12";
attr.payload.type = NVTX_PAYLOAD_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT64;
attr.payload.value.u64 = ((uint64_t)b << 32) | (uint64_t)aseq; // packed
nvtxRangeStartEx(&attr);
// ... selector logic ...
nvtxRangeEnd(nullptr);
```
Use packing if we want smaller attribute blobs.

dana: Also add a small telemetry counter metric we can expose in console: `selector.fallback.count` by route/model so we can alert when fallback rate spikes.

alice: OK I'll do the NVTX naming as `KS:pick=...,b=...,aseq=...,rmx=...` (colon + comma, no spaces), add a sampling flag default 0.1 for detailed attrs, and emit lightweight root span always. I'll include the perfetto link and kernel_map diff in the PR.

ben: Thanks — ping when the PR is up and I'll run the microtrace on the dedicated pool.

alice: will do. Thanks all.
